name: icestorm
desc: Tools for analyzing and creating Lattice iCE40 FPGA bitstream files
why: Reverse-engineered tools for Lattice iCE40 FPGA bitstreams open the door to actually reading and writing hardware configurations.

brief.what_it_is: Project IceStorm is a set of command-line tools for analyzing and creating bitstream files for Lattice iCE40 FPGAs. The README describes it as documenting the bitstream format and providing simple tools for analyzing and creating those files. The tools include icebox_asc2hlc, icebox_chipdb, icebox_hlc2asc, icebox_vlog, icepack, icepll, iceprog, icetime, iceunpack, and others listed in the package. The brief does not show each tool's inputs and outputs in detail, since I did not read their individual pages. Bitstream files are the input and output for most tools, and iceprog uploads a binary to the FPGA over USB.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says the project aims at documenting the bitstream format of Lattice iCE40 FPGAs and providing simple tools for analyzing and creating bitstream files. The docs ask 'Why the Lattice iCE40?' and 'What is the Status of the Project?' as their opening questions, but I did not read those answers.
brief.how_it_works: The docs index lists per-tile documentation for the FPGA fabric: logic tiles, IO tiles, RAM tiles, and UltraPlus features such as DSP tiles, SPRAM, and the RGB LED driver. It also covers the bitstream file format, CRAM and BRAM organization, and CRC checks. The tools are built on that reverse-engineered documentation. I did not read the detailed pages, so I cannot say more about the mechanism.

commands_seen.context: Appears in a docs troubleshooting heading about the error "Can't find iCE FTDI USB device (vendor_id 0x0403, device_id 0x6010)" when uploading code to the FPGA. It shows that iceprog takes a binary file and programs it to the board.

brief.install_notes: The docs index has separate install-related pages: 'Where are the Tools? How to install?', 'Notes for Installing on OSX', 'Installing FTDI Library', and troubleshooting pages for 'iceprog make error on "ftdi.h not found"', 'yosys make error on "<tuple> not found"', and the 'Can't find iCE FTDI USB device' error. Together these suggest building from source, needing the FTDI library for iceprog, and an FTDI USB device on the board. I did not read those pages, so the exact steps are unknown. The brew formula description did not give install caveats.
brief.standout: It is a fully open reverse-engineering effort. The iCE40 bitstream format was documented by reading the chip, and the tools are the working output of that. Together with Yosys and nextpnr, it forms a fully open-source FPGA flow.
brief.status: unknown. The README and docs index show no release date, last commit, or maintenance note. I could not check the repository's commit history or releases.
brief.caveats: I did not read the individual tool pages or the install pages, so commands, usage, and setup steps are not verified. The README says 'Most of Project IceStorm is licensed under the ISC license', which implies some parts may carry other licenses. Building from source and FTDI driver setup look error-prone according to the troubleshooting headings. Hardware needed: an iCE40 board with an FTDI USB interface, implied by the iceprog error.
